requirement: Before using a source, its current terms/auth/limits are verified and recorded in the source register with date and link.
Every source is accessed via a connector implementing `SourceConnector`; the rest of the app never imports source-specific code.
External calls are made server-side only, with an identifying User-Agent and required contact/mailto/API-key parameters.
Rate limits are enforced client-side below the documented maximum; HTTP 429/5xx use exponential backoff with jitter (max 3 retries).
Each connector has a timeout (default 8 s), circuit breaker, and returns structured errors; one failing source never fails a federated search.
Federated search responses include `source_status` per source and label partial results.
DOIs are normalized (lowercase, no URL prefix); invalid DOIs are rejected into the import/ingest report, not stored.
Missing fields are stored as `NULL`; no inference or fabrication of metadata, authors, or abstracts.

`works.provenance` records `{source, fetched_at}` per populated field; field-level conflict resolution uses trust order: Crossref (bibliographic fields) > OpenAlex > PubMed (biomedical) > others; user edits outrank all.
Abstracts delivered as inverted indexes are reconstructed deterministically; abstracts are length-capped and sanitized (no HTML injection).
Identifier upserts are idempotent (unique DOI/PMID/OpenAlex id); concurrent ingests do not create duplicates.
Fuzzy dedup uses the thresholds in SKILL.md P7; scores and decisions are stored; auto-links are reversible.
Errata/corrections/retraction notices and preprint↔published pairs are linked via relation, never silently merged.
Responses are cached with per-source TTL (default search 1 h, work 7 d, citations 24 h) and a cache key containing normalized params.
Citation graph expansion is lazy, depth ≤ 2, and capped (default 200 nodes) with "load more".
Pagination uses the source's cursor mechanism; deep paging beyond a cap (default 1,000 results) is refused with guidance to refine the query.
Connector tests use recorded, scrubbed fixtures covering success, empty, malformed, 429, and timeout; a nightly live smoke test is non-blocking.
No scraping of sites that disallow automated access or forbid it in terms; adding a new source requires an ADR.

An optional BASE (or similar broad multilingual) connector may be added only after its access policy and reuse rights are verified (DAT-001) and an ADR is written; sources feeding topic maps must expose title, abstract, language, and year or be flagged incomplete.
Support import of RIS, BibTeX, CSV (with column mapping), and CSL-JSON.
Imports run as background jobs with progress and are idempotent per file hash + project.
Parsing enforces limits: file ≤ 25 MB, ≤ 50,000 records, 60 s CPU; violations produce a clear error.
Every import yields a parse report (imported/skipped/error with reason and line ref) stored and downloadable.
Records match to existing works by DOI/PMID, then fuzzy rules; unmatched create minimal works flagged `source=import`.
Enrichment never overwrites user-provided fields; it fills nulls only.
Dedup candidates enter a review queue; merge stores `merge_snapshot`; undo restores exact prior state.
Collections (tree), tags, and notes are project-scoped and soft-deletable.
Export in RIS, BibTeX, CSL-JSON, CSV; round-trip preserves title, authors, year, venue, DOI, abstract, keywords.
User file uploads validate MIME by content sniffing, size ≤ 50 MB, AV scan, and are stored in private object storage with sha256.
Text extracted from user files is chunked into project-scoped chunks only (`scope='user_file'`).
Citation formatting uses CSL styles via a maintained CSL processor; ≥ 5 common styles bundled.
Imported text is treated as untrusted: sanitized for display; URLs inside are never fetched server-side.
Zotero import via user API key or file; keys encrypted at rest; feature optional.
Library list supports 5,000 items with server-side pagination, sort, filter; p95 ≤ 1.5 s.
Deleting an item/file is soft first, hard-purged within 30 days; export includes user notes.

PDF uploads offer `extract_only` mode: after successful extraction the original is deleted and only derived data is kept; deletion is verified and audited; failed extractions purge the file within 24 h.
Each review project has a versioned protocol; screening is disabled until protocol v1 exists.
Protocol edits create a new version; every decision stores `protocol_version`.
Stages `title_abstract` and `full_text` are supported; items advance per `state-machine.md`.
`screening_decisions` and `screening_resolutions` are append-only (DB grants enforce); corrections use `supersedes_id`.
Exclude decisions require a reason from the controlled list; project may add reasons; global defaults seeded.
Blind mode hides other reviewers' decisions and AI suggestions at the API level until the caller has decided on that item/stage.
Roles enforced server-side: owner (all), reviewer (decide), viewer (read).
A verdict mismatch among required reviewers creates a conflict; unresolved conflicts block stage completion.
Conflicts are closed only by a resolution row from an authorized resolver; reviewers' original decisions remain.
Raw agreement and Cohen's kappa are computed per stage from the log; kappa is undefined (shown as "n/a") when expected agreement = 1 or n < 2 reviewers.
PRISMA 2020 flow counts are computed from import batches + decision log; no manual overrides.
PRISMA endpoint verifies reconciliation (identified − duplicates = screened; screened − excluded = assessed; assessed − excluded = included) and returns discrepancies when violated.
Full-text exclusion counts are broken down by reason in the PRISMA output.
AI suggestions include rationale mapped to protocol criteria, model name, prompt hash; stored separately from decisions.
AI suggestions are never applied automatically and never count as a reviewer; UI labels them "suggestion".
Record whether each human decision matched the displayed AI suggestion (for transparency, never to coerce).
Screening UI supports keyboard shortcuts, resume, undo-last (via superseding row), and meets WCAG 2.2 AA.
Decision log export (CSV) includes item id, DOI, stage, reviewer, verdict, reason, timestamp, protocol version.
Retrieval queries for private scopes always include `project_id` filtering; cross-project retrieval is impossible by construction and covered by a 2-tenant test.
Chunking is section-aware, 300–500 tokens with ~15% overlap; chunk text, ordinal, section, and `embedding_model` stored.
Indexing jobs are idempotent and resumable; model change triggers versioned re-embedding without downtime.
Retrieval is hybrid (FTS + vector) with reciprocal rank fusion and a reranker; ranks and scores are stored per run.
A sufficiency gate refuses when distinct works < N (default 3) or top rerank score < threshold; refusal lists what was searched.
Per-study extraction returns the defined fields with supporting chunk ids; absent info is `null`, never inferred.
Users can edit extractions; edits set `edited_by_user` and are tracked.
Synthesis output is validated JSON of atomic claims; each claim has ≥ 1 citation id from the retrieved set; invalid output gets one repair attempt then fails closed.
Every claim is independently verified against only its cited chunks; verdict stored and displayed.
Claims with `unsupported` verdict are removed from the answer or clearly flagged; `partially_supported` are flagged.
Citation integrity gate: every cited chunk → work exists; retracted works are flagged; DOIs shown when known.
Retrieved text is delimited and treated as untrusted; synthesis/verifier/extraction models have no tool access.
Prompt-injection tests (malicious abstracts) pass: injected instructions do not alter output format, leak prompts, or add uncited claims.
LLM/embedding calls go through provider-agnostic adapters with timeouts, retries, token/cost accounting.
Per-user weekly quota and global monthly budget enforced before work starts; clear message on exhaustion.
On LLM failure, return retrieval-only results (ranked works/chunks) with an explanatory notice.
Runs persist question, retrieval config, chunk ids/ranks, model names, prompt hashes, tokens, cost, claims, verdicts; prompts/completions text not logged.
A golden eval set (≥ 100 items incl. unanswerable and adversarial) runs nightly and pre-release; thresholds from `05 §5`.
Streaming progress via SSE (retrieving, extracting, drafting, verifying).
Any aggregate "agreement" display lists all underlying studies, N, designs, and a method disclaimer; otherwise not shown.
Each journal data field's source and licence/terms for storage and redisplay are verified and recorded before ingestion.
Journals store `data_as_of` and provenance per field; UI always shows source and date for metrics.
Journal search supports filters: category/field, quartile (if licensed), indexing (DOAJ etc.), OA, APC (none/≤ amount), language, country, publisher, free text.
Hard filters apply before scoring; filtered-out journals never appear.
Match input is title + abstract (+ optional keywords); max 6,000 characters; input is not stored unless user saves it to a project.
Score components (semantic, keyword/topic, citation affinity) and weights are returned and displayed; weights configurable server-side.
Each recommendation lists ≥ 3 similar recent articles from that journal with DOIs when available.
UI/API never show acceptance probability or guarantees; copy reviewed against a disclaimer list.
Quality signals are factual and verifiable (indexing, OA model, APC); no "predatory/safe" labels; verification guide shown.
Submission checklist items cite source URL/line; unverifiable items are marked "verify manually".
Data older than 12 months is visibly marked stale; refresh jobs scheduled.
Offline eval set (≥ 60 labelled abstracts) tracks top-5 hit rate; regression below threshold blocks release.
All AI-generated/modified content is visibly labelled with model, date, and verification status.
Every AI feature call writes `ai_usage_log` (feature, stage, model, purpose, human_reviewed) without content text.
Users can mark AI outputs as human-reviewed; the flag feeds disclosure statements.
The disclosure generator uses the usage log and templates, is editable, and states that journal-specific AI policies must be checked.
Reference-check job resolves DOIs/references, compares title/year/first author, and reports verified / unresolved / mismatch / retracted per item.
Reference checks never auto-modify the user's references; changes require explicit confirmation.
Retraction/correction status is checked via the registered data source, shown with check date in library, search, synthesis.
Writing-assist modes are limited to outline, critique, language editing, structure checks; no fabricated data/references/peer-review text.
No feature is built to evade AI detectors or conceal AI use; requests are declined with an alternative.
Unpublished manuscripts/uploads are private-scoped, excluded from logs and global indexes, not used for training, deleted on request within SLA.
Provider settings for retention/training opt-out are recorded in `docs/subprocessors.md` and checked in release checklist.
A Coverage Notes panel lists sources searched, known gaps, and AI limitations; included in exports.
UI copy reminds authors they remain accountable for all content and citations.
Disclosure and labelling features have automated tests; copy reviewed for no compliance guarantees.
Outputs of mapping, positioning, and gap analysis use relative wording ("in the analyzed set"), never claim novelty/first/no prior work, and automated copy scans enforce this.
Every map/lineage run has an explicit scope (search result set or library subset); scope, parameters, seed, embedding model, and code version are stored in `map_runs`.
Runs are capped (default 500 records); larger scopes are refused with guidance; records lacking a title are excluded and reported.
Runs are deterministic: identical inputs, parameters, seed, and models produce identical clusters/lineage (tested).
Cluster labels derive from metadata keywords (deterministic c-TF-IDF); optional LLM labels are constrained to the cluster's keyword set, marked AI-generated, and logged per ETH.
Clustering uses multilingual embeddings so mixed-language sets work; record language per item and show language mix.
Topic map UI sizes clusters by member count, supports click-through lists and "add cluster to library", exports PNG/SVG/CSV, and offers an accessible table/list alternative.
Lineage edges use only in-set evidence: citation, semantic similarity, keyword/concept overlap, chronology; each edge stores its component scores.
Chronology hard rule: a parent's year ≤ child's year; same-year links require citation evidence.
Confidence bands (High/Medium/Low) follow `algorithms.md`; Low confidence yields "Needs review" and no auto-assigned parent.
Families are produced by the documented algorithm with a minimum size (default 3); others are "Unplaced"; roots are identified by rule, not guessed.
The audit table lists every paper with branch, parent, evidence types, confidence, status, and missing-metadata flags; it is sortable, filterable, searchable, and CSV-exportable.
Every visual placement (map, tree, lineage) links to its audit row and stored evidence; nothing is rendered without evidence.
User overrides of parent/branch are allowed, tracked (who, when, previous value), keep machine evidence unchanged, and can be reset.
Data-quality gaps (missing abstract, DOI, year, references, keywords) are flagged with reason codes and surfaced in the table.
Manuscript positioning returns closest family, top-3 parent candidates with component scores, and shared vs distinctive concepts; copy says "closest in the analyzed set" and never claims novelty.
Manuscript text is processed in private scope; `retain_text=false` by default; only derived vectors/results persist; deletion on request; never logged.

The gap view emits typed signals (unresolved condition, future-work, lineage gap, data-quality), each with source work, ≤ 300-character excerpt from open-access or user-owned text, and extractor version; a persistent banner states a gap is not global novelty.
The module never generates related-work prose; optional AI may only rewrite evidence summaries, labelled and logged per ETH-001/ETH-002.
Botanical tree, lineage map, and table views share one analysis without recomputation; lineage diagram exports to SVG/PNG using our own visual language.
Monorepo layout per `repo-layout.md`; `make dev` boots all services; health endpoints (`/healthz`, `/readyz`) exist.
API is contract-first: OpenAPI is updated before implementation; CI verifies implementation ⊆ contract.
Config is read from environment, validated at boot (Pydantic Settings); production refuses dev defaults/empty secrets.
Alembic migrations are reversible, tested up/down, and non-destructive via multi-step patterns.
Backend follows router→service→repository boundaries; no cross-module imports except through service interfaces.
Errors use RFC 7807 with stable `code` and `request_id`; no stack traces or internal ids leak.
Auth uses single-use, 15-min magic links, secure/httpOnly/sameSite cookies, session rotation, CSRF protection, rate limits.
Authorization (owner/reviewer/viewer) is enforced server-side in services; deny by default; covered by role-matrix tests.
Background jobs are idempotent with `dedupe_key`, bounded retries, status API, and cancellation where applicable.
JSON logs with `request_id`; OTel traces across API→worker→connector→LLM; user content and secrets never logged.
List endpoints use cursor pagination with max page size (default 25, max 100).
Static quality gates: ruff + mypy (strict on new code), ESLint + TS strict; failures block merge.
UI supports `en` and `id` via ICU message catalogs; no hard-coded user-facing strings; locale-aware dates/numbers.
Frontend meets WCAG 2.2 AA on core screens; axe checks run in e2e.
Frontend uses generated API client; every view has loading, empty, and error states; optimistic updates only for non-audit actions.
Performance budgets: initial JS ≤ 250 KB gz per route, LCP ≤ 2.5 s on mid-tier mobile profile.
Risky features sit behind feature flags with documented rollback.
README, runbooks, ADRs, `.env.example`, and `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md` are updated with each relevant change.
`/me/export` and `/me` DELETE are implemented end-to-end with job status and tests.
Dependencies are pinned by lockfile, minimal, preferably ≥ 14 days old; additions need justification (and ADR for frameworks/services).
CI runs lint, type-check, unit, integration, and build on every PR; main protected.
Lint/type failures block merge (ruff, mypy, ESLint, tsc).
Unit coverage ≥ 85% on core modules (dedup, normalization, kappa, PRISMA, parsers, scoring).
A script verifies every MUST requirement ID in scope has ≥ 1 test named `test_<ID>_*`; missing coverage fails CI.
Secret scanning runs pre-commit and in CI; leaked secrets block merge and trigger rotation.
Shared fixtures exist: two tenants, role matrix users, recorded connector responses, golden RAG set loader.
Integration tests use real Postgres+pgvector and Redis (testcontainers).
Every migration is tested upgrade→downgrade→upgrade on a populated fixture DB.
Tenant isolation tests prove no cross-project reads/writes in library, screening, retrieval, synthesis, files.
Role-matrix tests cover owner/reviewer/viewer for every project route.
Connector tests use scrubbed fixtures (success, empty, malformed, 429, timeout).
schemathesis (or equivalent) runs against the OpenAPI contract; no 5xx and no schema violations.
Playwright e2e covers search→import→dedup→screen→PRISMA→synthesis→export and auth flows.
axe-core runs on core screens; no serious/critical violations.
SAST, dependency audit, and container scan run in CI; high/critical findings block unless an ADR accepts risk with expiry.
DAST baseline (e.g., ZAP) runs on staging per release; findings triaged.
k6 load tests meet PRD latency targets for search, decisions, and synthesis queueing.
AI evals (SYN-018, JRN-012) run nightly and pre-release; threshold regressions block release.
Metrics/alerts exist for error rate, queue depth, connector errors, LLM cost/quota, latency, cert expiry.
Backups verified by a documented restore test at least quarterly; RPO/RTO documented.
Release checklist executed and recorded; rollback plan documented and rehearsed on staging.
Retention jobs, export, and deletion flows implemented and tested; sub-processor list current.
Runbooks exist for connector outage, LLM outage, queue backlog, cost spike, data deletion request, security incident.
Security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protections), cookie flags, and rate limits are asserted by automated tests.

Golden mapping fixtures (determinism, chronology rule, cluster NMI, lineage top-1/top-3, evidence integrity, wording scan, manuscript privacy) run in CI and pre-release; threshold regressions block release.
